preamble: Devoicing of the bilabial implosive to [p]. In the Pearic languages Chong and Pear, Proto-Austroasiatic *ɓ appears as p (*ɓic 'to lie down, sleep' > Chong pìc, Pear pic), where Bru keeps b (bếq). Headley (1985) reconstructs Proto-Pearic *buːl 'drunk' with *b, and the step Proto-Pearic *b > p is filed under b > p. In Katuic, the Chatong dialect of Ngeq has p with a breathy vowel where Bru, Ta'Oi and Katu keep b: Proto-Katuic *ɓic 'lie down, sleep' > pi̤c, *ɓool 'drunk' > po̤ol, *ɓaam 'chew' > pa̤am (Sidwell 2005). Chatong devoices the plain voiced stops in the same way (*dal 'prop up' > ta̤l, *kduŋ 'bag' > katṳŋ), so *ɓ probably merged with *b first, but no stage with b is recorded for Chatong. Chatong keeps b in baar 'two' < *ɓaar and in beec < *-ɓeec, and after a presyllable (kabom < *kɓoom, kabɨp < *kɓip). Khmer reached p in two attested steps: Proto-Austroasiatic *ɓaːr 'two' > Old Khmer ពិរ៑ bir > Modern Khmer ពីរ /piː/. These are filed under ɓ > b and b > p. Modern Khmer ɓ and ɗ are secondary, from earlier *p and *t (បី 'three' < Old Khmer ⟨pi⟩ [ɓiː] < *peːʔ; ដៃ 'hand' < *t₁iiʔ), so the two series swapped places.
phoneticEffects: Devoicing, Loss of Implosion, Airstream Change

examples.note: Ngeq (Kriang) keeps b (bool). Chatong keeps b in baar 'two' < *ɓaar and in beec (baar beec 'corners of the mouth') < *-ɓeec, and after a presyllable: kabom 'hold in the mouth' < *kɓoom, kabɨp 'close the mouth' < *kɓip.
